terms.comment: The two churches’ Creed differs here: the Latin Church confesses the Spirit quī ex Patre Fīliōque prōcēdit, the Orthodox Church, with the Greek text of 381, as proceeding from the Father (τὸ ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς ἐκπορευόμενον).
Greek παράκλητος, the one called to help.

paraclitus.html: The Clementine Vulgate’s and the Roman Breviary’s spelling (Jo. 14.26), from Greek παράκλητος with η said as ī; the Stuttgart Vulgate prints paraclētus (Latinitas Precēs, Notae).

phrases.latin: in nōmine Patris, et Fīliī, et Spīritūs Sānctī
phrases.english: in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit

phrases.latin: Paraclītus autem Spīritus Sānctus, quem mittet Pater in nōmine meō, ille vōs docēbit omnia
phrases.english: But the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things

sources: Lewis & Short: spiritus · Lewis & Short: sanctus · Lewis & Short: paracletus
